chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār said:
I asked him about a man who buys from the tax collector (ʿāmil) while he is oppressing (people), and he said: 'He buys from him as long as he does not know that he has oppressed someone in it.'

key_terms.الْعَامِلُ: The tax collector or governor responsible for collecting revenue

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy from a tax collector if he is unjust?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the principle of *istishab* (presumption of validity) in commercial transactions, ruling that ignorance of the seller's specific injustice (*zulm*) preserves the contract's integrity. It reflects the Shia juristic distinction between the moral status of the wealth and the legal validity of the trade, ensuring economic stability by protecting buyers from hidden defects in title.
